results.description_html:

Roadmap Milestone 4. The 3D counterpart to the 2D GCS, operating on component transforms rather than point coordinates.

Constraint set and DoF removed

  • Mate / Flush - normals antiparallel or parallel with coincident planes; removes 3 DoF (1 rotation, 2 translation).

  • Insert / Axis-to-Axis - cylindrical axes aligned and concentric; removes 4 DoF.

  • Angle - fixed angle between normals; removes 1 rotational DoF.

  • Distance - fixed separation along an axis; removes 1 translational DoF.

Scope

  • Face and axis reference picking that survives regen - depends on the topological naming work in M1-2.

  • A solver that adjusts ComponentInstance.transform matrices to satisfy all active constraints while leaving the remaining DoF free.

  • Over-constraint and conflict detection reported per constraint, mirroring the sketcher's DoF states.

Acceptance

  • A shaft inserted into a bore stays concentric when either part is dragged.

  • Conflicting mates are reported as a conflict, not silently ignored or solved to an arbitrary pose.

results.name: M4-1 -- Component registry and ComponentInstance with a typed Matrix4 transform
results.description_html:
Source: Documents/3d/road_to_catia.md

Roadmap Milestone 4, and the structural prerequisite for everything else in it.

Current state

There is no assembly layer at all - ComponentInstance, ComponentRegistry and mate constraints return zero matches across src/. Every solid is a top-level document entity; there is no notion of the same part placed twice.

Scope

  • ComponentRegistry mapping component id to definition; a definition holds either an in-session Document or a sourceFile path to a STEP part.

  • ComponentInstance with componentId, transform and constraints[].

  • Instancing: one definition, many instances, one tessellation.

Explicit constraint from the roadmap

transform must be a typed THREE.Matrix4, not a flat number[]. The roadmap calls a 16-element array with no enforced layout "a bug source at every matrix multiply". Note that Solid3D today stores position and rotation as loose {x,y,z} objects, so this is a deliberate departure from the existing pattern.

Acceptance

  • The same component placed three times shares one definition and one tessellation, with three transforms.

  • Assemblies round-trip through the persistence layer.

results.name: M3-2 -- True G2 continuity for loft and sweep via explicit boundary conditions
results.description_html:
Source: Documents/3d/road_to_catia.md

Roadmap Milestone 3. The roadmap is blunt about this one: do not conflate "smooth loft" with "G2 loft" in the UI or documentation.

The distinction

  • BRepOffsetAPI_MakeThruSections with SetSmoothing(true) yields G1 - matching tangent vectors. Light reflections break abruptly.

  • G2 requires matching the second derivative along the shared boundary, built with explicit compatible boundary conditions via GeomFill_BoundWithSurf or equivalent, specifying curvature-matching tangent frames at each profile.

  • Surface degree must be at least 3 in both directions.

Relationship to #41

#41 covers the loft operation itself (ThruSections through multiple profiles). This ticket is the continuity work on top, and should not start before #41 lands.

Acceptance

  • G0, G1 and G2 are selectable per loft, and the UI names them accurately.

  • A G2 joint shows unbroken flowing bands under the existing zebra shading mode; a G1 joint shows an angled break. Screenshot comparison recorded on the ticket.

results.name: M1-2 -- Topological naming Phase 1: semantic edge and face tags to replace the unused GeometricSignature stub
results.description_html:
Source: Documents/3d/road_to_catia.md

Roadmap Milestone 1. The hardest problem in the document, and the one the roadmap warns took FreeCAD nearly a decade.

Current state

FeatureNode.topologicalReference?: GeometricSignature is declared and never read or written anywhere in the codebase - the only occurrence outside its own declaration is the type itself (src/core/model/Solid3D.ts:132-146). GeometricSignature proposes matching on centroid, normal, area, faceType and faceIndex, i.e. geometric re-matching after the fact. Downstream features today bind to raw indices via faceMapping, which is exactly the failure mode the roadmap describes: change a sketch so the extrude goes from 4 faces to 6, and a fillet bound to edge 3 silently lands on the wrong edge.

Scope - semantic tagging, not index matching

  • Tag edges and faces by their generation semantics at creation time, e.g. Extrude_1_Face_3_Lateral_Edge_2, using the roadmap's rule that an edge is identified by the pair of faces that produce it.

  • Downstream features bind to the string token, not an index.

  • Unresolved bindings after a regen surface as an explicit warning and a reselection prompt - not a silent rebind. The roadmap accepts manual reselection as workable for v1.

  • Either populate GeometricSignature as a secondary disambiguator or delete it; a declared-but-dead field is worse than neither.

Acceptance

  • Editing a sketch so the extruded face count changes leaves the downstream fillet either correctly bound or explicitly flagged, never silently wrong.

  • A regression test covers the 4-faces-to-6-faces case named in the roadmap.

results.name: M1-1 -- Promote the per-solid FeatureNode list to a cross-entity feature DAG with dirty-flag partial regen
results.description_html:
Source: Documents/3d/road_to_catia.md

Roadmap Milestone 1. The foundation: without it, every later feature is direct-mode geometry that has to be torn out and rebuilt once history exists.

What is already there

This is not a greenfield build. Solid3D already carries features: FeatureNode[] (src/core/model/Solid3D.ts:140,162) with types Extrude, Cut, Fillet, Scale, Sketch, Chamfer, Shell and Draft, and Solid3DReevaluator.reevaluate() (src/core/engine/Solid3DReevaluator.ts:14, 319 lines) replays them - including re-solving linked sketches and re-deriving a revolve axis when the source profile moves.

What is missing

  • It is a linear list, not a DAG. Features are owned by one Solid3D and replayed in array order. There is no inputs[]/outputs[], so a feature cannot depend on two upstream bodies and a boolean of two histories cannot be expressed.

  • No dirty flags. reevaluate() replays the whole chain from baseBrepSnapshot every time. The roadmap is explicit that partial regen must be designed in from the start, not retrofitted.

  • No topological ordering pass - array order is assumed to be a valid execution order.

Scope

  • Lift FeatureNode out of Solid3D into a document-level graph with explicit inputs/outputs node ids.

  • Add dirty plus invalidate() that marks self and all downstream nodes.

  • Topological walk in REGEN; re-execute only dirty nodes.

  • Keep the existing per-feature execution logic in Solid3DReevaluator - it becomes the node execute() bodies rather than being rewritten.

Acceptance

  • Changing one parameter on a 20-feature model re-executes only that node and its descendants, proven by a counter exposed through the test bridge.

  • A boolean whose two operands each have their own feature history regenerates correctly.

  • Existing single-solid models still regen identically - this is a superset, not a replacement.

results.name: Phase C4 -- OutlineEffect is WebGL-only and draws every shaded frame
results.description_html:
Viewer draws every SHADED and ZEBRA frame through OutlineEffect (three/examples/jsm/effects/OutlineEffect.js), not through the renderer directly. That is where the black entity outlines come from, and those outlines are most of what makes the viewport read as CAD rather than as a game engine.

OutlineEffect is WebGL-only. It takes a WebGLRenderer, keeps its own material cache keyed on the renderer's internals, and re-renders the scene with inverted-hull materials. It cannot be pointed at a WebGPURenderer.

Found while typing the renderer seam in #161 — it is the single place the seam is deliberately broken, with a cast at the construction site. It is a hard blocker for #169: a WebGPU viewport either loses every outline or needs this replaced first.

Options

  • Ship WebGPU without outlines initially and treat it as a known parity gap. Cheapest, and honest, but the flagged WebGPU path would look visibly worse than WebGL, which makes it hard to evaluate.

  • Post-process outline pass — depth/normal edge detection in the node graph. Backend-neutral, better looking, and it is the same pipeline the GTAO work (#52) needs, so the two should be scoped together.

  • Keep the existing EdgesGeometry + LineSegments that the viewer already builds, and drop OutlineEffect on both backends. Worth measuring first: it may be that the explicit edge lines already carry most of the look and OutlineEffect is doing less than it appears.

Acceptance

  • A decision recorded here with a screenshot comparison, not just a preference.

  • Whatever is chosen works on both backends, or the gap is written down in #171.

  • The as unknown as THREE.WebGLRenderer cast in the Viewer constructor is gone, and effect is no longer any.

Goal

Move the real viewport onto WebGPU, behind a capability check, with the WebGL path kept permanently as a fallback. WebGPU coverage still has holes (older Safari, some Linux drivers, software rasterisation in CI), so this is a second backend, never a replacement.

Why it is worth doing

Raw FPS on a static CAD scene is not the payoff — the current bottleneck is CPU-side (tessellation, raycast picking, the Viewer.ts god class), not the GPU. The real wins are compute shaders: id-buffer GPU picking instead of CPU raycasting, GPU-side normals/LOD, and a TSL node graph that makes the post-processing work (GTAO, outline passes) writable once instead of twice.

  • Phase D — the swap. WebGPU behind a flag, automatic fallback, full re-validation through the test bridge.

  • Phase E — the payoff. GPU picking and compute-side mesh work.

Constraints

  • WebGL must keep working at every commit — no big-bang cutover.

  • WebGPU init is async (await renderer.init()); the current boot path constructs the renderer synchronously in the Viewer constructor. That asymmetry is the single largest structural change.

  • COOP/COEP are already set (vite.config.ts:97) for SharedArrayBuffer; nothing here may break the OCC worker.

results.name: UNDO reports success but reverts nothing - every command pushes an empty history transaction
results.description_html:
Found by driving the app through the new test bridge (#156) on 2026-07-27. This is the defect that blocks acceptance of the B-rep restore work (#20 / #138).

Symptom

Apply SFILLET to a solid, then run UNDO. The log prints Undo performed. and nothing is reverted. Pressing undo again changes nothing either - it never advances.

Measured on a box built from typed coordinates, one fillet, r=5 on edge 0:

  • Plain box: 8 vertices, 6 faces, 15505-byte B-rep, features [Box]
  • After one fillet: 10 / 7 / 19038, features [Box, Fillet]
  • After UNDO: still 10 / 7 / 19038 / [Box, Fillet], while the log said Undo performed.
  • After a second UNDO: unchanged again.

Reproduced identically two ways: through the bridge, and by dispatching real Enter keypresses on the #cmd input. It is not an artefact of the automation.

Root cause

Three things combine:

  1. App.handleResult (src/app.ts:2564-2567) wraps every dispatched action in startTransaction(this.doc.constraints) / commitTransaction(this.doc.constraints) - including actions that record no entity changes at all, such as finish and undo itself.
  2. HistoryManager.startTransaction (HistoryManager.ts:34) does if (currentConstraints). doc.constraints is an empty array, which is truthy, so currentConstraintsBefore is set to [] - non-null - on every single action.
  3. HistoryManager.commitTransaction (HistoryManager.ts:44) pushes when this.currentTransaction.length > 0 || this.currentConstraintsBefore !== null. Because of (2) the second half is always true, so every action pushes a transaction, even with zero records.

So finishing a command leaves an empty transaction on top of the real one, and UNDO pops that empty entry while its own wrapper pushes a fresh empty entry in its place. The stack read live from doc.history:

  • after BOX: [ADD]
  • after SFILLET on the edge: [ADD, TRANSFORM+ADD]
  • after the Enter that ends edge selection: [ADD, TRANSFORM+ADD, EMPTY]
  • after UNDO: [ADD, TRANSFORM+ADD, EMPTY] - unchanged
  • after a second UNDO: [ADD, TRANSFORM+ADD, EMPTY] - unchanged

Undo can never reach the real transaction underneath. Calling window.app.doc.undo() directly - outside the wrapper - does work, which is why the unit tests on #20 pass.

Make an empty transaction a no-op. results.name: Automation -- WebCAD Test Automation Bridge
results.description_html:
Problem

Playwright can only see the DOM and raw pixels. The MODELLING viewport is a single <canvas> painted by Three.js/OCC — there's no accessible tree for the cube, grid, gizmo, or snap markers. Playwright can click a pixel and screenshot, but it has no way to ask "is the front face selected?" or "did OSNAP trigger?".

Solution

Expose an in-app test bridge — a window.__webcadTest object — that gives Playwright a semantic API into the same state your renderer already has (camera, scene graph, selection, snap). Playwright drives this API via page.evaluate() instead of simulating mouse gestures blind. Mouse simulation is kept only for the handful of interactions that must genuinely go through real DOM events (e.g. regression-testing drag-select itself).

Bridge should be tree-shaken out of / disabled in production builds (guard behind import.meta.env.DEV or a ?testBridge=1 query flag) so it's zero-cost in prod.

Suggested build order

  1. Epic 1 (bridge shell + readiness) — unblocks everything else

  2. Epic 2 (camera) — highest immediate value, matches your "zoom/pan/perspective" ask directly

  3. Epic 3 + 4 (scene graph + selection) — matches "select object / select vertex"

  4. Epic 5 (command bridge) — cheap, since CommandProcessor already exists

  5. Epic 7 (snap state)

  6. Epic 6 (real input helpers) — only once 2–4 exist to derive coordinates from

  7. Epic 8–9 (regression + example suite)

results.name: Undo/redo does not restore solid B-rep state (OCC worker cache goes stale)
results.description_html:
Corrected 2026-07-26 — this issue was originally filed on a false premise. It was created as "No undo/redo system implemented anywhere in the app". That was wrong: a full undo/redo system exists and works.

Evidence undo works: CommandManager.ts:231 maps "UNDO" to {action:'undo'}; SystemHandler.ts:47-54 handles it via doc.canUndo() / doc.undo() / context.syncFromDocument(); Document.undo() is at Document.ts:160. Confirmed end-to-end in the browser — running UNDO logs "Undo performed." and an erased entity comes back. There is now an e2e regression test covering this (tests/e2e/grip_edit.spec.ts → "Undo").

The real defect, which is what this issue now tracks: HistoryManager.undo() accepts an onSolidBRepRestore callback (HistoryManager.ts:87) and calls it to push a stored brepSnapshot back into the kernel (:139-140, and :210-211 for redo). But Document.undo() passes undefined in that slot (Document.ts:168), and Document.redo() does the same (Document.ts:183). The restore path is therefore dead code.

Consequence: undoing a fillet / shell / chamfer restores the entity object but leaves the OCC worker holding the post-operation shape, so the kernel and the document disagree from that point on. This is exactly what the original issue #20 described — that issue was valid and has been reopened.

Fix: pass a real onSolidBRepRestore from Document.undo() and Document.redo() that hands the snapshot to the kernel. Now feasible because brepBytes is returned on every op (see the resolved brepSnapshot issue).

Done when: filleting a solid, undoing, then performing another boolean uses the pre-fillet shape.
